text: Folders whose names end in .al bypass the folder handling (FileSaved instead of DirChanged).
evidence: Mapping rule 9 sends PathChanged for every path under the root, whatever its extension; reconcile rule 4 decides file vs folder by fs::metadata, and any folder goes through the one folder rule. T6(c) moves an x.al/ folder in.

text: NotFound alone does not prove removal (folder replaced by a file, file replaced by a folder).
evidence: Reconcile classifies by stat: NotFound or NotADirectory means absent; every affected vp (nested included) not found by the stat or the subtree walk is removed (rules 4-5). T6(a) and T6(b).

text: Case-only renames are unsound through the case-insensitive fallback; root containment must be normalized first (round 2).
evidence: rel_under_root compares normalize_path forms of root and p before anything else (mapping rules 5-6, reconcile rule 1) and keeps the disk case in rel; T10 row. Case matches: reconcile rule 3. T7.

text: Cache watch registration had a loss window; a successful retry must resync before notifying (round 2).
evidence: Order rule: resync runs before any DepsChanged it causes; a retry that succeeds runs resync and THEN sends DepsChanged/Overflow. T11(b) and T11(e).

text: Creating or removing a .git boundary changes the cache set but was not handled.
evidence: Withdrawn by the conductor's round-2 scope narrowing: a .git-boundary move is a stated limit (Non-goals, ledger line 46; Discoveries). The ancestor walk is fixed at watcher start, as the loader saw it.

text: The global-config folder lifecycle stayed blind (absent at start, replaced, removed).
evidence: Withdrawn by the conductor's round-2 scope narrowing: live reload of the GLOBAL config is a stated limit (Non-goals, ledger line 45; Discoveries).

text: Race between the initial read and the watcher start; parents must be registered before scope discovery (round 2).
evidence: Narrowed to root and cache folders: start registers the root and walked_dirs first, then the existing candidate folders, then config install and build. T11(a), T12(a).

text: Tests pinned helpers, not production wiring; raw .al source forwarding was unpinned (round 2).
evidence: T12(b) pushes a raw Modify(Data) for Alpha.al through the fake backend, handle_raw, the updater and on_swap, and asserts a higher generation and republished diagnostics; break: drop the PathChanged forwarding in handle_raw.

text: T8's all-disabled half could not fail; the no-compute_all claim was not observable.
evidence: T12(d) is a separate test: default config publishes the Extra() hint, then all detectors off must send one empty notification (break: the old early return at server.rs:606-608).

text: F5 assumed typed events; Modify(Any) and EventKind::Any on folders were dropped.
evidence: Rule 9 sends every kind but Access (and Data/Metadata on non-.al paths) to PathChanged, and the folder rule does not depend on the kind; F5 covers the remaining Data/Metadata assumption. T10 rows.

text: F12 reintroduced a second copy of the folder rule.
evidence: F12: if the refactor moves the closure digest or a dependencies test, fix the single enumerator; never keep the old walk beside a new one; otherwise stop and revise.

text: A fingerprint-equal save is not a no-op (parse plus a rung-1 generation).
evidence: Reconcile rule 6: a known file found by a folder walk is read only when its stamp moved, and plans nothing when its text is equal. Editor saves keep their rung-1 apply (updater.rs:2076-2113, perf_support_smoke.rs:176,207).

text: cargo test -- --list proves the inventory, not the outcomes.
evidence: The salsa proof diffs the sorted per-test outcome lines of cargo test -p al-sem --lib before and after, plus the whole suite and goldens.

text: The watcher thread's wiring (reload call, real watch registration, resync, source forwarding) is pinned by no test.
evidence: T11 drives the production WatchState::handle_raw with a recording fake (registration order, resync before send, retry, AppFile, inside-root cache); T12(b) takes a raw .al event to the published snapshot; T12(c) drops the reload call.

text: T8's second half cannot fail: nothing is left to clear.
evidence: Fixed with S9: T12(d) is a separate test from the default config (hint published) straight to all-disabled.

text: FileRemoved still trusts the event kind and never checks the disk.
evidence: The watcher emits only PathChanged (rule 9); classify reconciles PathChanged, FileSaved and FileRemoved from disk alike, independent of kind (ledger line 105). Existing FileRemoved tests delete the file first (probe row). T8.

text: A case-only rename yields Remove and Save of one vp, and the result depends on their order.
evidence: Reconcile rule 3 splits unknown identity (Overflow), same file (Overflow for PathChanged), different file (own vp) and absent p; rule 7: plans are keyed by vp and, when one vp is observed twice in a classify call, the later observation wins deterministically. T7(a) both orders.

text: An event naming the root itself would re-parse the whole workspace, or wipe it.
evidence: Mapping rule 6: Structural on the root's own entry -> Overflow, Touched -> nothing; reconcile rule 1: p is the root -> Overflow. T10 rows.

text: An RwLock read held across compute_all can block code lens behind a waiting writer.
evidence: Readers clone the config under the lock and release it before any work.

text: The config test depends on the developer's global ~/.al-sem/config.json.
evidence: T12 writes every detector key explicitly in .al-sem.json (as server.rs:2094-2104 does), so the global file cannot change the outcome.

text: Drop rows passed with their rule deleted; a positive .app -> DepsChanged row with a production-path break was missing (round 2).
evidence: T10 has a positive Create(File) <root>/<cache>/x.app -> DepsChanged row (break: delete the AppFile arm); T11(f) sends the same raw event through the production handle_raw.

text: The design did not list the docs and tests that go stale.
evidence: Paragraph lists updater.rs:105-108, :179-186, :1005-1011, the renamed :1844-1874 test, watcher.rs :139-151 and the FileChange test, server.rs :70, :785-830, :1220-1230.

text: Wrong citations (OUTSTANDING range, the two allow lines, the dependencies tests range).
evidence: Probe row separates watcher.rs:115 (try_recv) from server.rs:126 (updater_handle, stays put); OUTSTANDING 712-720; dependencies tests 1606-1769.

text: The lock delta does not show feature unification.
evidence: Probe P2b: only hashbrown 0.17.1 (via indexmap) and portable-atomic lose features; al-sem names neither; /work/bench/160-13/p2/pkgfeat*.diff.

text: The ConfigChanged flag is lost at break decision, and a failed rung 3 drops it.
evidence: The flag is carried out of the inner loop with the decision; a rung 3 returning None with the flag set calls on_swap(&cur, Full). T9.

text: Normalizing the whole path makes the .app test case-blind on Windows, unlike the loader.
evidence: Only folder parts are normalized; is_app_file (case-sensitive, as dependencies.rs:425) runs on the raw file name. T10 row: X.APP is not DepsChanged.

text: Startup permits competing config writers: the initial install can overwrite a newer reload.
evidence: ConfigHandle stores (config, reloaded); install_initial writes only while reloaded is false, so a startup-time reload always wins. T14 tests both orders.

text: Duplicate-watch mode merging is undefined (root equals home could downgrade the root to non-recursive).
evidence: The home watch is gone; the one remaining collision (a root that is itself a candidate folder) is handled by 'Recursive wins'. T11(g).

text: The injected home does not reach config loading, so a global-config reload cannot be tested.
evidence: No longer applies: global-config reload is out of 13a (Non-goals, ledger line 45) and no test claims a global reload; workspace-config tests write every detector key explicitly (O7).

text: Existence roles fire on Windows' untyped Modify(Any) folder events, causing endless full rebuilds and republishes.
evidence: The Structural/Touched split now governs only rules 4 and 6: a cache folder outside the root sends DepsChanged only on an existence change or a Structural kind; inside the root only on a Structural kind; the root's own entry sends Overflow only on a Structural kind; .git is dropped outright (rule 8). T10, T11(c).

text: A folder's untyped event re-reads every indexed file under it.
evidence: The one folder rule walks the subtree and stats each file; a known file is read only when its stamp (len, mtime, plus dev/ino on Unix) moved. Stamps live in Updater.stamps, empty after each full build and set only from a stat taken before an updater read (S4N1), so a folder is read once after a rebuild and then only where stamps moved. T13(a) counts one read per file, then zero.

text: On a case-sensitive FS a new target.al beside a known Target.al is never indexed.
evidence: Reconcile rule 3 uses the case fallback only when p and root.join(K) canonicalize to the same file, or p does not exist; a different existing file is its own vp; unknown identity -> Overflow. T7(b).

text: Structural evidence can disappear during coalescing (replacement followed by a touch).
evidence: PathChanged carries no kind; reconcile depends only on disk and stamps, so any events for a path in any order reconcile to the same plan. T13(d) runs replacement-then-touch through spawn_updater against a fresh build.

text: Touched-folder deletion misses entire child subtrees.
evidence: Removal rule 5: every known vp anywhere under rel(p)/, nested subtrees included, that the subtree walk does not find is removed. T13(c) moves src/sub/ out.

text: T12(c) loses its diagnostic precondition after (b) clears the hint.
evidence: T12(c) is now a separate test on a fresh fixture that first asserts the Extra() hint is published, then disables unusedProcedures.

text: F17 converts unknown identity into proven difference, creating duplicates.
evidence: Reconcile rule 3: a canonicalize failure on either side while p exists -> Overflow; a failed rebuild keeps the old snapshot (updater.rs:642-662). F17 rewritten. T7(e) injects a one-sided failure through a test seam.

text: F5 no longer repairs its stated failure shape: a same-name folder replacement seen only as Touched skips changed files.
evidence: The folder rule is kind-independent and re-reads every file whose stamp moved, so a same-name replacement is re-read whatever event arrives; F5 now only widens forwarding, which fully repairs it. T6(d), re-run as Modify(Data) under F5; T13(e).

text: A Touched folder re-walks .al-free child folders (notably .git) on every event.
evidence: Mapping rule 8 drops every path with a .git component under the root, nested repositories and submodules included (stated divergence from the build walk); the direct-child walk clause is gone, and a folder event walks only that folder's subtree with stats, no reads of unchanged files. T10 .git rows.

text: The forced unwatch/re-watch must apply only to cache folders outside the root.
evidence: Rule 4 splits CacheFolder: outside the root -> resync / forced re-watch on Structural; inside the root -> DepsChanged on Structural, no unwatch/watch. T10 row and T11(i).

text: Post-build stamp seeding can permanently certify stale text: a folder replaced between the build's source read and the stamp seeding gets its NEW stamp recorded, so later folder events never re-read it.
evidence: Stamps paragraph: no post-build seeding; the stamp map starts empty after every full build, and a stamp is set only from a stat taken before a read the updater makes, paired with that read's text. Post-build metadata never certifies snapshot text. inputs.rs is unchanged (carrying build-read stamps would need a field through WsFile, SourceFile and ParsedFile); the cost is one read per known file on the first folder event after a rebuild. T15 replaces src/ between the build's read and the updater start, delivers only folder events, and compares to a fresh build (break: post-build seeding).

text: Stamps recorded during classify survive a batch forced to rung 3 whose rebuild fails, vouching for text that was read but never indexed.
evidence: New 'Staged stamps' paragraph: stamps taken during classify are staged with the plan and committed only when it is applied (rung 1, rung 2, or a no-op batch whose text equals the published snapshot); a rung-3 batch discards them, and a failed rebuild keeps the old snapshot and the old map. T15(b): failed rung 3 then a folder event re-reads a.al (break: commit stamps during classify). Placed as its own paragraph so no other anchor's text changed.

text: Overflow never reloads the diagnostics config: a lost .al-sem.json event followed only by a rescan leaves ConfigHandle stale.
evidence: Round 7: the Overflow arm reloads the config AND sends ConfigChanged with Overflow (also on a root back through retry), so a failed rebuild still republishes with the reloaded config. t11l asserts Sent(ConfigChanged) before Sent(Overflow); break: drop that send -> log without Sent(ConfigChanged).

text: Overflow does not repair cache registrations: a cache created while events were lost is loaded but never watched.
evidence: Round 7: overflow recovery re-arms every registered outside cache folder (a registered entry may hold a dead native watch), then resyncs new ones. t11l second rescan: break drop the cache re-arm loop -> Unwatch(parent/.alpackages) missing.

text: Replacing the workspace root loses its recursive watch permanently (same as C2).
evidence: Round 7: the root is never a cache candidate to the watch (outside_candidates excludes everything under or at the root), so its recursive mode and its own retry are never touched by resync; a structural event on it maps to rule 6 (Overflow -> re-arm). T11(g): a refused re-arm stays in `failed` as Recursive. Break: restore the old filter -> T11(g) fails (root re-armed by the cache path).

text: Windows special-input matching stays case-sensitive: APP.JSON / .AL-SEM.JSON events miss their arm.
evidence: map_event compares the normalized rel (identity on Linux, lowercase on Windows) for .al-sem.json, .al-call-hierarchy.json and app.json. New #[cfg(windows)] test t10_windows_special_names_in_another_case: not runnable here (no Windows CI, ledger note).

text: One cache's existence change suppresses another cache's replacement re-arm.
evidence: The structural re-arm runs whatever resync returned. Test t11m_replaced_cache_is_rearmed_while_another_appears; break `structural && !changed` -> Unwatch(a) missing.

text: A root that is itself a candidate is re-registered NonRecursive on a structural event.
evidence: Round 7: same fix as F3: resync never registers or clears the root, so it cannot downgrade it to NonRecursive nor drop its retry. T11(g) pins both.

text: The production loop's 5 s retry scheduling is not pinned.
evidence: retry_failed itself is pinned (T11(e), t11k). Pinning the loop's timer needs an injectable clock, machinery the design did not ask for; the call site is three lines.

text: T15(b) protects apply_batch, not the spawn_updater rung-3 arm.
evidence: The spawn_updater rung-3 arm never commits the staged stamps (they are dropped with the tuple); a thread-level test needs a sleep between two batches to avoid coalescing, a flaky shape. Recorded, not built.

text: Startup-race coverage tests only the ConfigHandle, not the RootState call site.
evidence: Same as the task-3 review's F7 ledger note: T14 pins install_initial; the call site has no interleaving test. A deterministic one needs a hook inside the watch thread between registration and the install; not built.

text: canon() compares texts, decl ids, edge counts and incoming callers, not full edges, witnesses or event links.
evidence: The reconcile tests pin which files and texts end up indexed; full per-rung edge equality is the job of tests/lsp/lsp_incremental_parity.rs. Strengthening canon is a test-only improvement, not a correctness gap.

text: The completed salsa item still says the derives survive and removal is future work.
evidence: Rewritten as a completion note.

text: The watcher CHANGELOG line omits the stamp and failed-registration limits.
evidence: The line now states the same-length-and-mtime limit, the 5 s retry limit and the Windows folder-walk cost.

text: Two OUTSTANDING entries still name the deleted AlFileWatcher (same as C8).
evidence: Both now say "a stop signal for the watch loop (`watcher::start_watching`)" (lines 600 and 631).

text: "files replaced without their own event are reconciled" over-claims (same-length, same-mtime replacement).
evidence: Merged with F12: the limit is stated in the line.

text: There is no Windows CI; Windows-only tests run nowhere automated.
evidence: Ledger note under Not delivered names the tests and asks for one Windows run before a release.

text: reconcile looks for a case twin only in cur.parsed, so a new file reached under two spellings in one batch becomes two vps.
evidence: The plans of the batch are searched for a case twin, but only when the exact spelling is neither published nor planned (round 7, F2N1). Test c1_new_file_saved_under_another_spelling_in_one_batch_is_one_vp; break `&& false` -> got [..., newfile.al, NewFile.al].

text: The root removed and re-created leaves its recursive watch dead (same as F3).
evidence: See F3 (root kept out of the cache lifecycle) and the Overflow arm (re-arm root, re-arm caches, resync, reload, ConfigChanged).

text: On Windows every child change fires the folder's Modify(Any), so the updater walks (and after a full build reads) that folder's subtree.
evidence: Stated limit: the design accepted it (S2) with the measure-first fallback F16; no Windows machine here to measure. Ledger note and CHANGELOG line.

text: On non-Unix FileStamp is (len, mtime): an mtime-preserving same-length copy is not re-read.
evidence: Design stated limit F16 (content hash is the fallback, measure first on Windows); now also in the CHANGELOG line.

text: observe treats only NotFound from the read as absent; NotADirectory keeps a ghost vp.
evidence: The read uses is_absent like the stat. No test: the stat-to-read race window cannot be reproduced deterministically.

text: T12 waits at most 1000 ms for a publish on a loaded debug build: flaky.
evidence: An expected publish now waits up to T12_WAIT (5 s); the negative 300 ms wait is unchanged. The tests' breaks are unchanged.

text: handle_raw re-runs resync for each DepsChanged on top of the cache branch's own call.
evidence: Design S4: a DepsChanged from any source triggers resync first, so the rebuild never reads a cache folder that is not watched. The cost is one stat per candidate (at most 9) per such event, no reads.

text: OUTSTANDING still names AlFileWatcher (same as G1).
evidence: See G1.

text: Comments still describe an R3b Salsa layer that no longer exists.
evidence: The four comments (3083, 3126, 3668, 4139) no longer mention it.

text: rel_posix is computed twice per event: two O(N) scans of known vps.
evidence: rel_posix is O(path components), not a scan of known vps; the only scan of known vps is classify_path's, once per event, and only on an exact-key miss.

text: The C1 batch-twin lookup overrides an exact known spelling: with twins Target.al and target.al indexed and target.al deleted, [PathChanged(Target.al), PathChanged(target.al)] leaves target.al indexed.
evidence: An exact published or planned spelling wins before the batch twin search (`exact` guard). Tests f2n1_deleting_a_case_twin_upper_event_first / _lower_event_first assert rung 2 and equality with a fresh build; break `(!exact || true)` -> upper-first left: Some(One), lower-first left: Some(Three) (rung-3 fallback).

text: Every overflow re-arms the root recursive watch, a full tree walk on the watch thread during heavy churn (inotify overflow drops no watch on Linux). Cost only.
evidence: Correctness first: overflow is rare, and the re-arm (root and caches) is what F2/F3 need, since a registered entry may hold a dead native watch and the backend does not say which. Narrowing it to structural root events would reopen F2.
